netMetering: Net metering: exported kWh are credited against the kWh you buy, settled monthly. Turn it on only if your contract does that. Paid per exported kWh (e.g. a Smart Export Guarantee tariff)? Leave it off and enter the sell price on each zone — exports are valued at it either way.
sellRatio: Share of the buying price paid for an exported kWh when the zone has no own selling price. 0.7 = 70 % of the buying price. With net metering on, the hub also banks this share of a surplus month's kWh into the credit.
zoneRatio: Share of the kWh exported in this zone that become a credit against future purchases. 1 = every exported kWh cancels one bought.
defaultZone: Applies in hours and days no zone takes. Without one, energy in such hours is not priced.
zoneDays: The zone applies only on the ticked days. Where zones overlap the hub picks the more important one: peak over day, weekend over weekdays.
role: What the sensor measures: the input (the whole house from the grid), solar or another source, a single load. The role drives the flow diagram, money and advice.
phase: Which input phase this sensor's line is on. It sets the reference voltage and how the line's load is split across the input's phases.
partial: The hub did not record the whole hour or day — it was off or restarting. The value is right for the time it ran.
notBought: Solar energy the house used itself. It did not have to be bought — valued at the period's average buying price.
closedRecords: The hub writes the totals of each hour, day and month after it ends. The running hour is added when it ends; the Overview already counts it from the live counters.
point: Where a current is measured: the input, a line or an appliance. A point is an rbAmp module channel with a name, a role and history.
input: The point through which energy comes from the grid into the house or plant. Purchase, export and money for everything are counted by it.
line: A point on one load or a group of loads after the input: kitchen, heat pump, machine. Lines show where the energy goes.
zone: Hours with one price, e.g. day and night. Zones and prices are set in Tariffs.
unmetered: The input minus the sum of the lines: what loads without their own point use.
standby: The power the house draws when «everything is off»: power supplies, chargers, devices on standby. Counted from the quietest night hours.
